newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-ALBERT DENIES CHARGES, WILL BROADCAST PLAYOFFS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-ALBERT DENIES CHARGES, WILL BROADCAST PLAYOFFS.

text.p: Famed sportscaster Marv Albert, appearing in public Thursday for the first time since he was charged with sexually assaulting a woman, said he was innocent and would continue broadcasting the NBA playoffs.
"I would like to reassert my innocence and reiterate that all the charges against me are false and will be proven false in a court of law," a subdued Albert told a crowded news conference.
"I will continue my work with the NBA, NBC Sports and MSG network while I establish my innocence in a public courtroom."
At the brief news conference, Albert and his lawyers said due process had not been followed in the case, which became public Tuesday after the broadcaster's indictment Monday in Arlington, Virginia.

The 53-year-old sportscaster was charged in Arlington Circuit Court with one felony count of forcible sodomy and one misdemeanor count of assault and battery after the alleged incident in an Arlington hotel room on February 12.
Attorney Gerard Treanor said Albert had not been interviewed by police, prosecutors or the grand jury that indicted him.
Treanor said Albert would appear in court next Tuesday morning at his arraignment and plead not guilty.

One of the most recognisable voices in American sports broadcasting with his trademark "Yesss!", Albert will call Saturday's third game of the Eastern Conference finals between the Chicago Bulls and Miami Heat for NBC, the network said in an earlier statement Thursday.

Albert and his lawyers declined to answer questions at the news conference in a Manhattan hotel that was also attended by the sportscaster's four adult children. He is divorced and is engaged to be married again.

Police said Albert allegedly became enraged with the 41-year-old woman, threw her on the bed, bit her violently on the back 15 times and forced her to perform oral sex. New York newspapers quoted police sources as saying the woman had refused Albert's request to join him for sex with another man.
Forcible sodomy carries a penalty of five years to life in prison and assault and battery is punishable by up to 12 months and a $2,500 fine.

Albert also broadcasts for the Madison Square Garden Network in New York, where he is famous as the decades-long commentator for the New York Knicks of the NBA and the New York Rangers of the National Hockey League.
